The image is a microscopic view showing:

- A dense, dark central mycelial mass
- Numerous round, black spherical structures (sporangia) scattered throughout and on the periphery
- Long filamentous sporangiophores radiating outward from the center, each terminating in or bearing a round black sporangium
- Classic "pin mold" morphology under transmitted light

These structures are the hallmark of **Rhizopus** species: large, round black sporangia borne on sporangiophores arising from a dense mycelial mat. No other class in this list produces this distinctive morphology. Alternaria would show club-shaped multicellular conidia; Botrytis (Gray Mold) would show grape-like clusters; Sclerotinia would show hard sclerotia — none match this pattern.
